Mönchengladbach''', better known as '''Borussia Mönchengladbach''' ({{IPA|de|boˈʁʊsi̯a mœnçn̩ˈɡlatbax|lang|De-Borussia Mönchengladbach.ogg}}){{Cite book |title=Deutsches Aussprachewörterbuch |last1=Krech |first1=Eva-Maria |last2=Stock |first2=Eberhard |last3=Hirschfeld |first3=Ursula |last4=Anders |first4=Lutz Christian |publisher=Walter de Gruyter |year=2009 |isbn=978-3-11-018202-6 |location=Berlin |pages=383 and 753 |language=de}}{{Cite book |title=Das Aussprachewörterbuch |last=Mangold |first=Max |publisher=Dudenverlag |year=2005 |isbn=978-3-411-04066-7 |edition=6th |location=Mannheim |pages=212 and 560 |language=de}} and colloquially known as just '''Gladbach''', is a professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Mönchengladbach]], North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. The club plays in the [[Bundesliga]], the top flight of [[Football in Germany|German football]]. Nicknamed ''Die Fohlen'' {{IPA|de|diː ˈfoːlən|}} (The Foals), the club has won five league titles, three [[DFB-Pokal]]s and two [[UEFA Cup]] titles.[http://www.bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2008/index.php?f=127774.php News – Bundesliga – official website] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120418101224/http://www.bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2008/index.php?f=127774.php |date=18 April 2012 }}. Bundesliga.de. Borussia Mönchengladbach was founded in 1900, with its name derived from a Latinised form of [[Prussia]], which was a popular name for German clubs in the former [[Kingdom of Prussia]]. The team joined the Bundesliga in 1965 and saw the majority of its success in the 1970s, where, under the guidance of [[Hennes Weisweiler]] and then [[Udo Lattek]], a young squad with a fast, aggressive playing style was formed.{{Cite web |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/blmd22v-double-interview-yann-sommer-and-timo-horn.jsp |title=Rhineland derby double interview: Yann Sommer and Timo Horn – bundesliga.com |access-date=17 August 2016 |archive-date=26 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230426145812/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/blmd22v-double-interview-yann-sommer-and-timo-horn.jsp |url-status=dead }} During this period, Mönchengladbach won the Bundesliga five times, the [[UEFA Cup]] twice and reached a [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] final in [[1976–77 European Cup#Final|1977]]. Since 2004, Borussia Mönchengladbach have played at [[Borussia-Park]], having previously played at the [[Bökelbergstadion]] since 1919. Based on membership, they are the fifth-largest club in Germany with over 75,000 members in 2016{{Cite web |url=http://www.rp-online.de/sport/fussball/borussia/borussia-moenchengladbach-hat-jetzt-75000-mitglieder-aid-1.5903553 |title=Borussia hat jetzt 75.000 Mitglieder |date=14 April 2016 |publisher=RP Online}} and 93,000 as of 2021.{{Cite web|url=https://www.statista.com/statistics/595935/german-bundesliga-clubs-member-numbers/|title=German Bundesliga clubs membership numbers 2021|website=Statista|access-date=22 April 2021}} The club's main rivals are [[1. FC Köln]], against whom they contest the [[Rhine derby]]. Their secondary rivals include [[Borussia Dortmund]], [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] and [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]]."}}
